sentiment.rationale: The document shows genuine operational momentum: Boeing swung from a full-year free cash flow usage of $4.4B in 2021 to a positive $2.3B in 2022, and Q4 free cash flow was $3.1B versus $0.5B a year ago. Management reaffirmed 2023 guidance (unchanged from November) and reiterated long-term 2025/2026 free cash flow target of ~$10B, with confident language about being 'well positioned' and 'on the right path.' However, guidance was not raised, and structural risks remain (supply chain instability, 787 abnormal costs, BDS execution challenges), preventing a higher score.

summary.revenue: Q4 2022 revenue $19,980 million, up 35% year-over-year. Full year 2022 revenue $66,608 million, up 7% year-over-year.
summary.eps: Q4 2022 GAAP loss per share ($1.06), core loss per share (non-GAAP) ($1.75). Full year 2022 GAAP loss per share ($8.30), core loss per share (non-GAAP) ($11.06).
summary.guidance: Reaffirming 2023 guidance: operating cash flow $4.5-$6.5 billion, free cash flow $3.0-$5.0 billion. Long-term 2025/2026 objectives unchanged: ~$100B revenue, ~10% operating margin, ~$10B free cash flow.
summary.margin: Q4 2022 GAAP operating margin (1.8)%, core operating margin (non-GAAP) (3.3)%. Full year 2022 GAAP operating margin (5.3)%, core operating margin (non-GAAP) (7.0)%.
key_risks: Supply chain instability causing production stoppages and constraints.
787 abnormal costs increased by ~$600M to ~$2.8B total due to supplier constraint slowing production rate ramp.
BDS margins impacted by supply chain constraints, labor instability, and adverse cost accrual timing.
737 MAX 7 and 10 certification still ongoing; no exact certification dates provided.
China MAX deliveries uncertain; management will not predict timing.
BDS fixed-price development contract losses (e.g., $3.5B loss from operations for full year 2022).
key_opportunities: Strong demand across portfolio: 808 net orders in 2022, backlog grew to $404 billion.
737 MAX production rate planned to ramp to ~50/month in 2025/2026 timeframe.
787 production rate planned to ramp to 5/month in late 2023 and 10/month in 2025/2026.
Global Services strong performance with 13.9% operating margin in Q4, driven by commercial recovery.
China MAX returning to service; 100 airplanes in inventory for China customers.
Defense portfolio opportunities: autonomy, digital thread, T-7A, F-15EX, KC-46A tanker.
